title: Ultra-Low-Loss Silicon Nitride on Sapphire for Broad-Transparency Nonlinear and Quantum Photonics
authors: Abdur-Raheem Al-Hallak, Shuai Liu, Kailu Zhou, Jiangnan Liu, Shawn Chen, James Hu, Ruhi Yusuf, Christopher Rodriguez, Maya Sarram, Yiming Lang, Zetian Mi, Zheshen Zhang
abstract: The field of photonic integrated circuits (PIC) has flourished in the past two decades, fueling numerous cutting-edge applications across sensing, networking, data interconnect, and quantum information processing. As a guiding material for PIC, Si$_3$N$_4$ has seen extensive use for its ultra-low loss, broad transparency, and diversity in implementation across both thin and thick films. Although the standard, traditional silicon dioxide (SiO$_2$) on silicon (Si) substrates that underpin the majority of Si$_3$N$_4$ photonics face drawbacks in the form of long-wavelength transparency limited by SiO$_2$, high-stress deposition for anomalous dispersion thick-film Si$_3$N$_4$, and leakage loss to the Si layer for low-confinement thin-film Si$_3$N$_4$. Featuring increased long-wavelength transparency into the mid-infrared, low-stress deposition of Si$_3$N$_4$, and a low index, this work investigates sapphire substrates as alternate hosts for Si$_3$N$_4$ photonics with greater spectral coverage and reduced fabrication complexity. This work presents a robust method of fabricating ultra-low loss photonic integrated circuits on a 500-nm-thick Si$_3$N$_4$-on-sapphire platform, exhibiting record-low losses below $0.1 \rm \;dB/cm$. Implemented using this process are high-Q microrings with intrinsic quality factors in excess of $4.5\times10^6$ and coupled-ring photonic molecules to support nonlinear gain. Leveraging the achievable low loss and high-Q, this work further reports the first demonstration of Kerr-comb and soliton generation on the Si$_3$N$_4$-on-sapphire platform. These advances in loss, quality factor, and soliton generation on this versatile, broad-transparency platform pave the way for future work in spectroscopy and quantum-enhanced sensing across previously prohibited spectral regions for Si$_3$N$_4$ photonics with reduced fabrication complexity.
summary: This research introduces a novel and superior platform for photonics by utilizing Silicon Nitride deposited on sapphire substrates, overcoming spectral and loss limitations of traditional silicon-based chips. The authors report achieving record-low propagation losses and high quality factors, culminating in the first demonstration of complex nonlinear phenomena like soliton generation on this versatile material system.
main_problem: The paper addresses the limitations of traditional silicon dioxide on silicon platforms for advanced photonics, aiming to create a superior platform for ultra-low-loss, broad-transparency nonlinear and quantum applications.
main_result: They successfully fabricated ultra-low loss photonic integrated circuits on a Si3N4-on-sapphire platform, achieving record-low losses and demonstrating Kerr-comb and soliton generation.
method: The work combines advanced semiconductor fabrication techniques (LPCVD deposition, annealing) with optical characterization methods (transmission spectroscopy, dispersion fitting) to test nonlinear optical phenomena.
model_or_system: The physical system is a 500-nm-thick Silicon Nitride (Si3N4) waveguide deposited on a sapphire substrate. This platform is used to create high-Q microring resonators and coupled-ring photonic molecules.
key_observables: Intrinsic quality factors ($Q_i$) up to $4.6 	imes 10^6$, ultra-low propagation loss ($< 0.1 	ext{ dB/cm}$), and the generation of Kerr-comb and soliton states.
important_parameters: Waveguide thickness (500 nm), operating wavelength range (1490 nm to 1630 nm), and coupling rates ($\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that TE-polarization is preferred due to lower bending loss compared to TM-polarization on this platform. Dispersion fitting for photonic molecules is limited to the second order.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometry of the Si3N4 on sapphire platform and shows simulated mode confinement and dispersion characteristics for TE and TM polarizations.
paper_structure: The paper details the advantages of the sapphire host, presents the fabrication process for the Si3N4-on-sapphire platform, characterizes the ultra-low loss and high-Q factors for different polarizations, and finally demonstrates nonlinear phenomena like comb and soliton generation.
why_interesting: The demonstration of soliton and comb generation on a highly transparent, low-loss platform opens avenues for quantum-enhanced sensing and spectroscopy in spectral regions previously inaccessible to Si3N4 photonics.
